title: Cheap food then and the falling dollar now
summary: Cobb recalls four-cent sausage and three-cent bread, and the talk turns to the dollar being worth 26 cents and the pointlessness of saving.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: But I want to say this to you, Stanley: During that time, you could go out if you want pan sausage, you could get it for four cents a pound. Get a loaf of bread for three cents. And we could get five pounds of pan sausage on the corner at the corner grocery store for 20 cents and feed a lot of people, in those days. But even then my grandfather didn't do it. He went another route and got it cheaper than that. Can you imagine? Four cents a pound, three cents for a loaf of bread.
I am telling you the factual truth about --
Well, look at the way prices have doubled in the last ten years of a lot of things.
Well, we'd go so far as to talk about prices, the American dollar, I just heard the other day that the American dollar now is worth 26 cents.
Twenty-six cents! So what are you getting for your money? Nothing.
(Unintelligible) IT'S THE SAME WAY WITH THE POUND
And wait another few more years, then it won't be worth nothing and what the heck you doing? You're out there knocking your brains out for nothing.

Well, of course, you know what it does do. It makes the idea of saving your money seem a bit stupid in a way because if you save a dollar today with the idea that you'll have that in ten years' time, in ten years' time it's --
Yeah, it's multiplied, but it's also lost so much value, you've got where you started.
